headline: You may get about $306 a month for groceries.
subhead: This is an estimate. The county decides.

blocks.title: Do this today
paragraphs: Apply on BenefitsCal. To send your application today, you only need your name, where you live and your signature. The rest can come later.
How: fill in “Your Information”, then sign and submit. You can leave the other sections for later.
Why today? Your first month counts from the day the county gets your application. Our estimate: an application sent on a weekday before 5 PM counts that same day.
Our estimate: if you send it now, it counts from Fri, Oct 2, and your first month may be about $296 for October.

blocks.title: Why you may qualify
paragraphs: Since June 2026, SF State bachelor's students taking 8 or more units meet CalFresh's student rule. Just say you're in a bachelor's program.
Financial aid, scholarships and student loans don't count as income.
Your rent is high compared to your income, so your estimate is the highest amount for your household size.

blocks.title: Your answers for BenefitsCal
paragraphs: BenefitsCal screen names are in English. Here is what to answer on each one, based on what you told us.

rows.question: Are you a college student?
rows.answer: Yes. Type your Social Security number and citizenship information yourself. GatorPlate never collects them.

rows.question: Who do you buy and cook food with?
rows.answer: Just me. The people I live with buy and cook food separately.

rows.question: In college? Which school? At least half-time?
rows.answer: Yes · San Francisco State University · Yes

rows.question: Which one fits you?
rows.answer: I'm in a bachelor's program. If it's not on the list, say in your interview: “I'm in a bachelor's program at SF State.”

rows.question: Jobs and pay
rows.answer: My job pays about $900 a month before taxes.

rows.question: Financial aid
rows.answer: List it if asked. It doesn't count as income.

rows.question: Rent
rows.answer: My share of the rent: $1,100 a month.

rows.question: Heating or cooling bill apart from rent
rows.answer: Answer yes if you pay one.

rows.question: Other bills (water, trash, electric, phone)
rows.answer: List the ones you pay yourself. Internet doesn't count.

rows.question: Money in cash and in the bank
Last steps
rows.answer: Answer the 3-day (emergency) questions honestly. Pick the county where you live. Save your application number.

blocks.title: What to have ready
paragraphs: A photo ID. Your student ID works.
Proof of your address, like a lease or a bill.
Pay stubs from the last 30 days, or a letter from your boss.
Usually not needed — keep them handy in case the county asks: your class schedule and your financial aid papers.
You don't need papers to apply. When the county asks, upload them in BenefitsCal. A clear phone photo works. Save the upload receipt.
Not sure how to send them? Call the county: (855) 355-5757.

blocks.title: Your phone interview
paragraphs: After you apply, the county sets up your interview. You can choose phone or in person. Plan for about an hour. A call may show up as “Unknown” or “Spam Likely.” Answer it.
No call yet? Call the county at (855) 355-5757, or talk to the SF State CalFresh coordinator.
Got a letter or a BenefitsCal message asking you to call? Call (855) 355-5757 (weekdays 8 AM–5 PM) before the deadline.
They will ask about: who you live and eat with, your job and other money, your rent and bills, your classes and financial aid, and anything that changed.
From today's answers: work pays about $900 a month.
From today's answers: your rent share is $1,100 a month.
Your rights: a free interpreter, an in-person interview if you ask, bringing anyone you want, a decision within 30 days, and at least 10 days to send papers.
Missed the call? You'll get a letter called “Notice of Missed Interview” (CF 386). Call (855) 355-5757 right away to set a new time. If you wait too long, you may have to apply again.
Asked for papers after the interview? Send them by the date on the request. You get at least 10 days.
Live outside San Francisco? Your own county handles your case. The phone numbers here are for San Francisco.

blocks.title: After approval
paragraphs: Your EBT card comes in the mail. Activate it before you use it.
Lost card? Call (877) 328-9677.
About 6 months in, the county sends a short report form called SAR 7. Fill it out and send it back by the date on the form.
About 12 months in, you renew with a form and an interview.
If your household's total income goes over $1,729 a month, tell the county within 10 days.
If you move, tell the county your new address so you get your letters.

blocks.title: Food today
paragraphs: Gator Groceries and the AS Food Pantry give free food to all SF State students, every week.
Where: Cesar Chavez Student Center, bottom floor (Rec and Dining Level). Hours change. See https://asi.sfsu.edu/gator-groceries.
Need meals now? SF State Basic Needs has emergency meal cards. See https://basicneeds.sfsu.edu/emergency-meals.

blocks.title: Talk to a person
paragraphs: SF State CalFresh coordinator (CalFresh Help Clinic, Basic Needs), Student Services Building, Room 301.
Email calfresh@sfsu.edu to book a time, or call (415) 338-1203. Hours: Mon–Thu 8:30 AM–5 PM, Fri 8:30 AM–4 PM.
Your case code: K7Q-2FM. Share it so they can find your answers.
San Francisco CalFresh (county): (855) 355-5757, weekdays 8 AM–5 PM.
In crisis? Call 988 anytime. In an emergency, call 911.

footer: GatorPlate never stores audio. We keep your answers, not the conversation.
We don't collect Social Security numbers, and we never ask about immigration status.
Student-built prototype — not an official SF State, county, or CalFresh service.
You apply yourself on BenefitsCal. The county decides.

programs.name: Medi-Cal
programs.line: Health coverage for doctor, hospital and prescriptions, at no cost for most students today. Check the health box on the same BenefitsCal application.
notes: If a parent claims you on their taxes, Medi-Cal may count their income too.
Same application as CalFresh. No second form.

prefill.question: Do you also want health coverage (Medi-Cal)?
How much do you earn from work each month?

programs.name: Clipper START
programs.line: Riding Muni or BART over breaks? Clipper START could save about $90–$440 a year. Gator Pass covers the semesters.
notes: With CalFresh you can choose "Verify instantly through CalFresh". The card comes by mail, usually within 30 days.

notes: CalFresh or Medi-Cal counts as proof. Pick one LifeLine phone company and apply through it.

programs.name: Tax credits (CalEITC, EITC)
programs.line: Maybe about $200 in tax credits at tax time. A free tax volunteer at SF State VITA checks whether you can claim it.
notes: The state credit works with an SSN or ITIN. The federal credit needs an SSN valid for work.
Haven't filed for 2025? You may still file and claim credits for free.
Tax credits like the EITC don't lower your CalFresh.
Based on the 2025 state tables (2026 not out yet) and your monthly pay all year. A credit amount, not your refund.

prefill.question: How much did you earn from work in 2026? Bring your W-2.
Did you live with a parent? Time away at school can count.
prefill.answer: Tell the volunteer. It decides who can claim the credit.
